One-dimensional label-box de-overlap packing (a smartAlign() port)

Source: R/smart-align.R
smart_align.Rd

smart_align() is an exact port of smartAlign() from circlize: given one-dimensional intervals (label boxes) sorted by position and allowed to overlap, it removes the overlaps by iterative clustering and packing. Overlapping boxes are merged into a cluster, the cluster is re-laid out inside its own span with the boxes placed end to end at their original widths, and the cluster is then shifted back towards its original midpoint, moving as little as possible while staying in range. Iteration stops when the number of clusters no longer changes.

Usage

smart_align(start, end, range = range(c(start, end)))

Arguments

start, end

Numeric vectors giving the left and right end of each label box, in any consistent unit (npc, data units, ...). The two vectors must have the same length. start must be sorted increasingly (an assumption of the algorithm, matching the reference implementation); for unsorted input call order() first, or use box_arrange(), which sorts by midpoint itself.

range

Numeric vector of length 2, the range the boxes may occupy (e.g. c(0, 1)). Defaults to range(c(start, end)).

Value

A data.frame with columns start and end, in the same row order as the input (row i is the new position of the i-th input box).

Details

The function is pure (it touches no environment and uses no random numbers), so results are reproducible.

There are only two differences from the reference implementation, both of them robustness improvements:

  • an empty input returns a zero-row data.frame (circlize::smartAlign() throws an error);

  • invalid input (unequal lengths, non-finite values, a bad range) raises a clear error.

Note that when the total width of the boxes exceeds diff(range) the overlaps cannot be removed: the cluster is centred (as in the reference implementation) and the result sticks out of range. Callers should check feasibility first (smart_stack() drops low-priority labels before calling this function).

See also

box_arrange() for the other packing algorithm (BoxArrange from ComplexHeatmap), which also accepts unsorted input; smart_stack() for the multi-row label engine.

Examples

# two slightly overlapping boxes: packed end to end
smart_align(c(0.10, 0.12), c(0.14, 0.16), c(0, 1))
#>   start  end
#> 1  0.09 0.13
#> 2  0.13 0.17

# four identical boxes: spread around the original midpoint
smart_align(rep(0.5, 4), rep(0.6, 4), c(0, 1))
#>   start  end
#> 1  0.35 0.45
#> 2  0.45 0.55
#> 3  0.55 0.65
#> 4  0.65 0.75

# non-overlapping input is returned unchanged
smart_align(c(0.1, 0.5), c(0.2, 0.6), c(0, 1))
#>   start end
#> 1   0.1 0.2
#> 2   0.5 0.6
